critique: The heterogeneous-block theorem proves the advertised marginal-preserving productization, classwise oracle risks, and exact finite-menu commitment SDP rather than merely supplying one-sided bounds. Its substantive boundary is the direct-sum kernel restriction: cross-block kernels receive only an exponentially indexed mass-simplex formulation, not an efficient characterization or productization theorem. The higher-rank theorem's “sharp finite-n additive trace-relaxation gap” is simply the difference between two computed optima rather than an analytic gap bound, and its polynomial support reduction is existential rather than algorithmic. The TL;DR and project framing accurately preserve these boundaries and do not claim that the coupled-kernel problem has been solved locally or polynomially.
